# Baruch Chapter 1 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 1

---

**1** These are the words of the book that Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hasadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon,

**2** in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans captured Jerusalem and burned it with fire.

**3** And Baruch read the words of this book aloud to Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and to all the people who came to hear the book —

**4** to the nobles and the sons of kings, to the elders, and to all the people, both small and great, all who were living in Babylon by the River Sud.

**5** And they wept and fasted and prayed before the Lord.

**6** Then they collected money, each according to his means,

**7** and sent it to Jerusalem, to the priest Jehoiakim son of Hilkiah son of Shallum, and to the priests and to all the people who were with him in Jerusalem.

**8** This was at the time when Jehoiakim received back the vessels of the house of the Lord that had been carried away from the temple, to restore them to the land of Judah on the tenth day of Sivan — the silver vessels that Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had made,

**9** after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had taken away Jeconiah and the princes and the captives and the warriors and the people of the land from Jerusalem to Babylon.

**10** They said: Here is money; use it to buy burnt offerings and sin offerings and incense, and prepare grain offerings, and offer them on the altar of the Lord our God.

**11** And pray for the life of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and for the life of his son Belshazzar, that their days upon earth may be as long as the days of heaven.

**12** And the Lord will give us strength and enlighten our eyes, and we shall live under the shadow of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and his son Belshazzar, and serve them for many days and find favor in their sight.

**13** Pray also to the Lord our God on our behalf, for we have sinned against the Lord our God, and his anger and wrath have not turned away from us to this day.

**14** You shall read this book aloud to make confession in the house of the Lord on the feast day and on the days of the appointed seasons.

**15** And you shall say: Righteousness belongs to the Lord our God, but to us belongs open shame, as it is this day — to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,

**16** and to our kings, our princes, our priests, our prophets, and our ancestors,

**17** because we sinned before the Lord our God.

**18** We disobeyed him and did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, or walk in the commandments that the Lord set before us.

**19** From the day when the Lord led our ancestors out of the land of Egypt until this present day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God; we have been careless and have not listened to his voice.

**20** And so the evils and the curse that the Lord commanded through his servant Moses — on the day when he brought our ancestors out of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey — have clung to us to this very day.

**21** We did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God in keeping with all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us;

**22** but each of us followed the desires of his own wicked heart, serving other gods and doing what is evil in the sight of the Lord our God.

---

## Council Notes

**On v.4 — "nobles" vs. "mighty ones":** EMET preserves "mighty ones" (dynasts); LOGOS and SOPHIA prefer "nobles" as more natural in English for the social class intended. PNEUMA renders "powerful men." Consensus: "nobles."

**On v.8 — the tenth of Sivan:** All agents retain this chronological note. The date is unusual and textually significant; no smoothing warranted.

**On vv.11-12 — Prayer for Nebuchadnezzar:** PNEUMA adds an interpretive note about "survival theology." The consensus text retains the verse without editorial comment; the theological tension is part of the text's witness. "Shadow" retained over PNEUMA's "shelter" — the Hebrew/Greek idiom of royal protection deserves preservation.

**On v.20 — "clung to us":** EMET and LOGOS retain the adhesion metaphor. Consensus adopts it. PNEUMA's paraphrase ("caught up with us") is more vivid but loses the stickiness image.

**On v.22 — "intentions/inclinations of his own wicked heart":** All agents agree on the general sense; "desires" (SOPHIA) chosen as most natural English while preserving the volitional element.
